full_judgment:
Khondker Musa Khaled J: This First Appeal at the instance of the plaintiff-Bank, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27-11-93 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District judge, Artha Rin Adalat), Mymensingh, in Mortgage Suit No. 34 of 1992. 

 5. Mr Zakir Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the trial Court has committed gross illegality in not decreeing the suit on a wrong assumption that the defendant had already paid the dues in respect of the sanctioned loan. He contends that the bank statement (Exhibit 13), confirmation letter of the defendant (Exhibit 12) and statement of cash credit account (Exhibit 13) are all uncontroverted legally acceptable evidence, which stand to show that the accumulated balance amount payable by the defendant against the cash credit was Taka 79,711.87 and those evidence are consistent with the claim of the plaintiff-bank as made out in the plaint. So, the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be modified allowing plaintiff's claim of money and interest thereon calculating from the date of filing of the suit till realization. 

 9. Therefore, we do not find any scope to reduce the due amount claimed by the plaintiff-bank. Consequently the findings and decision of the learned Judge of the trial Court having no basis in evidence, suffer from gross illegality and, as such, the same are not legally sustainable. The learned Judge of the trial Court ought to have decreed the suit in full. 

 12. In the result, the First Appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree 27-11-93 is hereby set aside. The suit is decreed in preliminary form with cost against the defendant. The defendant is liable to pay Taka 79,711.87 to the plaintiff-bank along with 5% simple interest thereon per annum to be calculate from the date of filing the suit till realization. The defendant is directed to pay the decretal amount within three months from the date, failing which, the plaintiff-bank shall be able to realise The money by selling out the mortgage property in due process of law.
